title: Health checks and restart policies for services
when: The user wants a crashed or hung service to be restarted automatically, and traffic sent only to instances that are ready to serve.
prompt:
Goal: Separate liveness and readiness endpoints, a health check that uses them, and restart rules that recover crashes without endless loops.
Steps:
1. GET /healthz returns 200 {"status":"ok"} when the process answers; no database call, so slow dependencies never cause restarts.
2. GET /readyz pings dependencies with short timeouts (under 1 s) and returns 503 naming the failing check when not ready or shutting down.
3. Both send Cache-Control: no-store, need no auth and skip access logs.
4. Dockerfile: HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=3s --start-period=20s --retries=3 CMD ["node", "healthcheck.mjs"]; the script fetches /healthz and exits 0 or 1, since slim images may lack curl.
5. Restart: restart: unless-stopped in compose, or Restart=on-failure and RestartSec=2 in a systemd unit.
6. Crash loop limit: StartLimitIntervalSec=60 and StartLimitBurst=5 in [Unit]; log the exit reason on crash.
Quality bar:
- A killed process serves again within seconds.
- A dependency outage marks it not ready without restarts.
- Checks are cheap enough to run every few seconds.
Pitfalls:
- Liveness that queries the database, so one blip restarts every instance.
- Restart=always with no start limit, hiding a broken release.
- Returning 200 before real requests can be served.
Verify:
- [ ] /healthz and /readyz return the right codes.
- [ ] HEALTHCHECK has interval, timeout and retries.
- [ ] Restart policy and start limits set.
- [ ] Scripts parse.
Output: health routes in server.mjs, healthcheck.mjs, the HEALTHCHECK line and the restart settings.

examples.input: my node api dies sometimes and stays down until I log in
examples.output: /healthz and /readyz routes, healthcheck.mjs, HEALTHCHECK every 15s, Restart=on-failure with StartLimitBurst=5
